# COR101 `misleading-inline-if-continuation`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

A one-line `if` continues its action on the next line.

## Why

`if (c) &` followed by an indented statement on the next line looks like a block `if`. Whoever adds
a second indented statement below expects it to be conditional too, and it is not. Use an
`if ... then ... end if` block when the action does not fit on the line.

## Reported

```fortran
if (verbose) &
  call report(state)
```

## Preferred

```fortran
if (verbose) then
  call report(state)
end if
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[COR101] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = COR101` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `C152` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
